chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi and Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Qunut is before the ruku', and if you wish, then after it. The correct way to understand his saying عليه السلام, "and if you wish, then after it," is that we carry it upon the case of making it up for one who missed it in its proper place, or the case of taqiyyah, because it is the position of some of the 'ammah.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection in a context of religious caution
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the Sunni majority / non-Shi'i masses in this context
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: making up an act after missing its proper place
key_terms.مَذْهَبُ: the legal position or doctrinal view
key_terms.مَوْضِعِهِ: its proper prescribed place or position

ai.seo_question: Is qunut performed before or after ruku' in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the ruling of qunut in salat (prayer), stating that its sunnah position is before ruku'. The allowance of performing it after ruku' is understood as applying either to making up a missed qunut or to taqiyyah, since that is the view held by some among the 'ammah.
